category_title: Chamorro 5th-grade student with ADHD and literacy struggles who equates reading with pronunciation
student_description: Juan is a 5th-grade Chamorro student who struggles with reading comprehension and writing, often rushing through tasks and fixating on penmanship rather than content. He becomes easily frustrated by unfamiliar texts and relies on guessing words from initial letters. However, he thrives when allowed to use oral retelling as a cognitive bridge and engages deeply with culturally familiar texts in collaborative, small-group settings.

criteria.rationale: Juan relies on oral retelling as a 'magic tape recorder' to process and remember information before he can successfully write or answer comprehension questions.
criteria.check: The tutor prompts Juan to listen to a text and orally retell it before asking him to answer comprehension questions or begin a writing task.

criteria.rationale: Framing writing as a full retelling rather than a summary or formal essay helps Juan bypass his anxiety about mechanics and gets his ideas flowing.
criteria.check: The tutor explicitly asks Juan to write down everything he can remember from beginning to end, actively directing his focus away from summarizing or mechanical perfection.
